entities.summary:
Domingo Fernández Navarrete was a Spanish Dominican missionary and archbishop who played a pivotal role in the Counter-Reformation in 17th-century Southern Europe.


Born in 1618, Navarrete rose through the ranks of the Dominican Order, eventually becoming the Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela in 1671.

His tenure was marked by a series of reforms aimed at reasserting Catholic authority and suppressing Protestantism in the region.

Navarrete's efforts were part of a broader effort to contain the spread of the Protestant Reformation, which had already taken hold in many parts of Europe.

Despite his efforts, Navarrete's legacy was complicated by the devastating impact of the Great Plague of 1680, which ravaged the Iberian Peninsula and led to widespread social and economic upheaval.

In the end, Navarrete's contributions to the Counter-Reformation were overshadowed by the rise of Enlightenment ideas and the decline of Catholic influence in Southern Europe.

"The Church must be reformed from within," Navarrete once said,"but I fear we are losing the battle against the forces of modernity."
